entry.title: Insurance AI — underwriting & pricing guidance
entry.description: DFS explains its expectations for insurers using AI and external consumer data in underwriting and pricing under existing insurance law.
entry.timing: Issued 11 July 2024. Agency guidance, not a newly enacted AI statute.
entry.appliesTo: Insurers authorized in New York, Article 43 corporations, HMOs, licensed fraternal benefit societies, and the State Insurance Fund.
obligations: Assess actuarial validity and unfair discrimination before use and after material changes; document testing and explanations.
Maintain governance, management oversight, model documentation, and vendor controls. Responsibility remains with the insurer.
Provide applicable adverse-decision explanations and relevant disclosures.
entry.enforcement: DFS may examine AI use and request reports under its existing insurance supervisory powers.
entry.limits: The circular addresses underwriting and pricing, not every stage of the insurance lifecycle. Its expectations should be read alongside binding insurance statutes and regulations.

entry.title: NYC public schools: 2026–27 AI-use policy
entry.bill: NYCPS AI and Screen Time Policy · 2026–27
entry.description: Student-facing generative AI is restricted by grade. This is a NYC public-school policy, not a citywide prohibition on AI.
entry.appliesTo: NYC Public Schools settings covered by the policy.
obligations: Grades 2K–8: student-facing generative AI moratorium. Grades 9–12: limited approved, supervised uses.
Preserve required accessibility and language-support tools; check the policy’s exceptions.
entry.enforcement: Implemented through NYCPS school and tool-approval processes.
entry.limits: Staff planning and student-facing use are different. Do not generalize this policy to every school or private workplace.
